s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic hematochezia in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: Loose bowel movements with mixed blood
Multiple rectal and sigmoid colon polyps with surrounding erythematous, eroded mucosa
key_facts: 13-year-old boy with T-cell lymphoblastic leukemia
Receiving maintenance therapy with 6-mercaptopurine, methotrexate, vincristine, and dexamethasone
Intermittent neutropenia and consistent lymphopenia
Denies abdominal pain, weight loss, rashes, arthritis, oral or perianal lesions
Stool studies negative for Clostridioides difficile, cytomegalovirus, and adenovirus
Colonoscopy showed multiple semisessile, nonbleeding polyps in the rectum and sigmoid colon
Histologic examination revealed eroded surface mucosa with reactive hyperplastic glands and mixed inflammatory infiltrate
Histiocytes contained numerous basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions positive on von Kossa and periodic acid–Schiff stains

shortlist.label: Malakoplakia
shortlist.why_kept: Histologic examination revealed basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions positive on von Kossa and periodic acid–Schiff stains, consistent with Malakoplakia

shortlist.label: Chemotherapy-induced colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is receiving maintenance therapy with 6-mercaptopurine, methotrexate, vincristine, and dexamethasone, which can cause colitis

shortlist.label: Neutropenic colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is intermittently neutropenic, which increases the risk of neutropenic colitis

shortlist.label: Cytomegalovirus-induced pseudotumor
shortlist.why_kept: Although stool studies were negative for Cytomegalovirus, the patient's immunocompromised state and histologic findings could be consistent with Cytomegalovirus-induced pseudotumor

shortlist.label: Graft-versus-host disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of T-cell lymphoblastic leukemia and is receiving immunosuppressive therapy, which increases the risk of graft-versus-host disease

raw.rationale: The presence of basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions in histiocytes that are positive on von Kossa and periodic acid–Schiff stains is characteristic of Malakoplakia, a rare inflammatory condition often associated with immunocompromised states.

rejected.label: Chemotherapy-induced colitis
rejected.why: While the patient is on chemotherapy, the specific histologic findings do not align with typical chemotherapy-induced colitis.

rejected.label: Neutropenic colitis
rejected.why: Neutropenic colitis typically presents with abdominal pain and significant neutropenia, which is not consistently noted in this patient's case.

rejected.label: Cytomegalovirus-induced pseudotumor
rejected.why: Stool studies and histologic examination did not indicate the presence of cytomegalovirus.

rejected.label: Graft-versus-host disease
rejected.why: There is no mention of a transplant or graft, making graft-versus-host disease unlikely in this context.
